editorial.headline: Indonesia’s IP Consultancy Opening Meets Bali’s PMA Block
editorial.standfirst: Nationally open to 100% foreign ownership across all business scales, this intellectual-property consultancy activity is blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this intellectual-property consultancy activity in Bali today. That is the practical starting point, even though the activity is nationally open to foreign investment with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. In Bali, it is blocked for PMA registration because, at the large-business scale, every listed scope carries Low or Medium-Low OSS risk. The block is attributed to the Bali moratorium of May 13, 2026.

The activity begins with filing and handling applications, then extends to other connected work in intellectual property. Its stated field is expansive but precise: patents, copyright, trademarks, geographical indications, industrial designs, integrated-circuit layout designs, trade secrets, and other intellectual-property matters. The list is explicit both in range and in its focus on applications and their handling. It also names intellectual-property consultancy offices and law offices within the scope. This is a defined consulting activity centred on the administration of intellectual-property matters.

At the national level, the activity is open to enterprises at every scale listed in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. Those labels establish a broad registration position for the activity itself, rather than limiting it to one size of enterprise. The national PMA status is TERBUKA, and the stated national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. For a foreign investor assessing the national position, the record therefore presents a fully open ownership ceiling.

Bali changes the operative answer. The restriction stated for the island is a block on PMA registration, triggered by the Low and Medium-Low OSS risk classification across every listed scope at the large-business scale. The relevant Bali moratorium is island-wide and permanent. Nationally open at 100%, the activity is still unavailable for PMA registration in Bali. The national position establishes the ownership opening; Bali’s position determines whether that opening can be used on the island today.
